text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- The number of Norwegian farms producing environmentally green products has grown by 30 percent every year recently. Now Norway has 1,350 farms producing foodstuff in accordance with ecological principles.
- The Christian People's Party wants to lower the wealth tax in order for citizens not to lose money on their bank savings.
- Norway beat Iceland 1-0 in Reykjavik in an international friendly soccer match on Sunday night. Jostein Flo scored.
- Norway used to be a leading nation in the construction of big car and passenger ferries, but today there is only one such shipbuilder in Norway -- Kvaerner Fjellstrand.
- Statoil, the state-owned Norwegian oil company, has launched a study into how the introduction of the euro will affect the company.
- Statoil plans to invest between 350 and 400 million dollars to expand its petrol station network in Poland to 150 by the year 2000 from 47 today.
- Pharmaceutical group Nycomed's share price has increased by 30 percent since the merger plans with Britain's Amersham were announced on July 1, but the share should be able to rise furhter.
